clue.text: Happen to be with a woman

parts.note: 'I happen to be' can be put as 'I am', giving the verb form AM
with means and, joining things together

explanation.surface: Someone is told they will chance to be in the company of a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word, but it supplies AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Amanda is a girl's given name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: Made sense, being ready to go in leaderless

indicators.note: leaderless says the phrase loses its first letter

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who is padded up is wearing leg pads, ready to go in to bat

explanation.surface: Something made sense once it was ready to begin without a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go in' is cricket for going out to bat; a batsman straps on leg pads first.
explanation.definitionFit: When an account adds up, it is consistent and makes sense.

clue.text: Pack one's cases right and there's loads of space

indicators.note: cases means encloses, so the letter for right goes inside

parts.note: in a pack of cards the one is the ace; with the 's this gives aces

explanation.surface: Someone packs suitcases and finds plenty of room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' looks like luggage but is a verb: ACES encases R.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres, used loosely, means a great deal of room, as in 'acres of legroom'.

clue.text: Plot to turn over rough male totty proves to be false

indicators.note: turning over a plot means reversing the word

parts.note: a bed is a plot in a garden, as in a flower bed

indicators.note: rough speech drops its aitches, so the H is lost

parts.note: totty is British slang for attractive people; male totty are hunks

explanation.surface: Someone plans to seduce some rough, sexy men, and it ends in disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' signals a dropped H, as in rough working-class speech where 'hunks' is said 'unks'.
explanation.definitionFit: To debunk a claim is to show it is untrue or exaggerated, to expose it.

clue.text: "No more pills!" — birth control campaigner

parts.note: to say 'no more' is to call a halt: stop
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so pills are Es

explanation.surface: A cry against contraceptive pills is attributed to a famous birth control campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads as a slogan about the Pill; really it is an order to stop taking ecstasy tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Stopes was a British pioneer of family planning who opened the first birth control clinic in Britain in 1921.

clue.text: Mark takes direction in daze

indicators.note: takes means accepts inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a trace is a mark left behind
N, for north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark gets directions while in a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name but means TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a dreamy, half-conscious state, like a stupor.

clue.text: Start of play in test — making things happen

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to prove something is to test it, as in proving ground
a play starts with its first act, Act I

explanation.surface: A cricket Test begins and the action gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' and 'test' suggest cricket; ACT I is the start of a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Proactive means taking the initiative and acting ahead of events rather than reacting.

clue.text: Cut joint — a quarter eaten

indicators.note: eaten means swallowed inside, so the letter goes in

parts.note: joint ownership is shared ownership
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A cut of meat has had a quarter of it eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' and 'Cut' suggest butchery; joint is an adjective meaning shared.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheared means clipped or sliced off, as fleece is from a sheep.

clue.text: Are Fiona and father repeatedly being punished for romance?

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of area, abbreviated a

indicators.note: being punished means being beaten, so these letters are knocked into a new order
repeatedly means the word father is used twice

explanation.surface: Are Fiona and her father being punished, over and over, for a love affair?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are' looks like a verb but is the metric unit A. 'being punished' shuffles FIONA with FATHER twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is a romance; the question mark admits the definition is loose.

clue.text: Prepared obstacles to hold back river

indicators.note: back says the held letters are read in the opposite direction
the two words together hold a run of letters spanning their join

explanation.surface: Obstacles have been made ready to stop a river from flooding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold back' reads as a single verb about damming, but it splits: 'to hold' finds REDO across 'prepaRED Obstacles' and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Relocated abroad and no longer in England

definitions.text: Relocated abroad and no longer in England

indicators.note: relocated means moved to a new place, so these letters are moved into a new order
the word and is no longer to be found in England, so its letters are taken out

explanation.surface: A job has been moved overseas and is no longer done in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer in' takes AND out of ENGLAND, leaving ENGL; 'Relocated' rearranges ABROAD plus ENGL. The whole clue also describes the answer, an outsourced post.
explanation.definitionFit: Being Bangalored is slang for having your job outsourced to India, named after the Indian tech city of Bangalore.

clue.text: Agree hosting small party for retirement is more likely than not

indicators.note: retirement is going back, so the built letters are read in reverse
hosting means having a guest inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to agree is to nod
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Agreeing to throw a small leaving party is probably going to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' and 'for retirement' make the whole clue sound like a farewell do; 'for retirement' actually turns the whole built string round, NOSDDO becoming the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, an odds-on chance is better than evens, so it is more probable than not.

clue.text: Stand opposite comedian Jack, perhaps

parts.note: to face someone is to stand opposite them
a card is an amusing, eccentric person, a joker

explanation.surface: Someone stands facing a comedian named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack reads as the comedian's name; it is really the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack is one of the court cards, alongside king and queen, so it is an example of a picture card.

clue.text: Sun's leader incites staff representative

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Sun's

parts.note: to incite is to prod into action, to poke
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: The editor of the Sun newspaper stirs up a union official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun's leader' looks like a newspaper boss; 'leader' only takes the first letter. 'staff' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesman is someone who speaks on behalf of a group, so a representative.

clue.text: Broke law digging round new street fixture

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
digging turns over soil, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone illegally digs up a street around a new installation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digging' rearranges BROKE LAW to KEBARLOW, and 'round' puts it around N. Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Barlow has appeared in Coronation Street since its first episode in 1960, making him a permanent feature of the show.

clue.text: Run in (Dave's first) for a bit of bacon

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word Dave's

explanation.surface: Dave pops in first to pick up some bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon has a tough outer skin, the part trimmed away from a rasher.

clue.text: Ignore left leaving formerly respected institution?

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for left departs from the word

parts.note: to blank someone is to ignore them deliberately

explanation.surface: A wry dig at an institution that has lost its good name.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a sly comment on banks' reputations since the financial crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks were once trusted pillars of society; the clue jokes that their standing has fallen.

clue.text: Sprout's something to eat, when standing a long time

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: grub is informal for food
an eon is an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A sprout is something you eat, after it has stood for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sprout' looks like a Brussels sprout, the thing to eat; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to begin growing or flourishing, as buds do, so it means to shoot or grow.

clue.text: Drunk looked at following poster, hoping to get reaction

indicators.note: following says the piece for looked at comes after the other

parts.note: a troll posts provocative messages online to stir up angry replies
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: A drunk stared at an online poster who was looking for a rise out of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poster' suggests a bill on a wall; it is someone posting online.
explanation.definitionFit: Trolleyed is British slang for very intoxicated, like 'legless'.

clue.text: Politician's bill abandoned — about time!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so these letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A politician's bill has been dropped, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reshapes BILL into LIBL, which goes 'about' ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Liberal is a member of the Liberal Party, a British political party, so a politician.

clue.text: Part of set in use, otherwise theatre's empty

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters are put another way
empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the outside pair

explanation.surface: A stage set is in use, though the theatre is otherwise deserted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests a stage set, but here it is a set of rooms, a suite.
explanation.definitionFit: An en-suite bathroom is attached to a bedroom, forming part of a suite of rooms.

clue.text: Country doctor may in turn take over

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: in turn means the word is turned round

parts.note: may and can both mean being allowed to
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A country doctor may take over a practice in their turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny principality on the French Riviera, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Finish holiday and leave

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
to be off is to leave, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: Someone ends a holiday and goes home.
explanation.definitionFit: To break off a conversation or engagement is to bring it to an end, to stop.

clue.text: Top man in command

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the best is the top one
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: The boss is the one in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man' reads as one phrase meaning the boss, and 'in command' as being in charge; in fact 'in' is the container signal and 'command' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in 'at the King's behest'.

clue.text: See 8
Ring sailor? No time, he complains

parts.note: to ring is to sound a bell; a bell is a ring

indicators.note: No says the letter for time must be absent from the word

parts.note: a yachter is someone who sails a yacht

explanation.surface: A telephone call to a sailor is refused for lack of time, and he grumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellyacher is a habitual moaner, someone who grumbles constantly.

clue.text: Cutting relief? Very, very keen

indicators.note: cutting into means going inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: aid is relief given to people in need

explanation.surface: Someone asks if cuts to aid funding are what a keen person wants.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'very' tempts you to read both as the definition; only the second is.
explanation.definitionFit: An avid fan is extremely eager or enthusiastic, so it means intensely keen.

clue.text: Rebuke — it's not acceptable with repressed women

indicators.note: repressed means held down within, so the letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: a no-no is something not acceptable

explanation.surface: A telling-off: it is wrong to keep women down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repressed' puts W (with) inside NONO to make NOWNO; W for women follows.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Now, now!' is a mild reproof, said to calm or chide someone.

clue.text: Settled on Bashful originally — what about Happy?

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it
originally points to the initial letter of Bashful

parts.note: to have lit on something is to have settled on it, as a bird lights

indicators.note: about says the word for what is turned round

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: Choosing between two of the Seven Dwarfs: Bashful was picked, so what about Happy?
explanation.walkthrough: Bashful and Happy suggest Snow White's dwarfs; Happy is the definition and Bashful gives only B.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree, a synonym for glad or merry.
